case.source_text:
Synthetic nurse note for software testing. No real patient data.

The driver says his hearing is adequate when both aids are working, although radio instructions become difficult after several hours and he sometimes removes the left aid because of discomfort; his supervisor reports missed instructions, while the driver attributes these to a damaged radio speaker. An unsigned worksheet states unaided better ear average 39 dB averaged over 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 kHz, but the driver remembers wearing at least one aid during testing and cannot confirm that the sheet belongs to the most recent appointment.

The same folder contains an earlier note stating bilateral hearing loss and another form marked Hearing: normal, with no explanation of whether the statements refer to aided performance or unaided testing. There is no current audiologist report describing functional hearing with the aids, and the nurse has not accepted the recalled test conditions or selected the more favourable entry as definitive.

His blood-pressure medicines were changed after BP 180/106 mmHg at a pharmacy last week, whereas today's BP 152/90 mmHg was measured only once; he reports occasional dizziness but no definite loss of consciousness. He is unable to establish a stable period on the new regimen, and neither the symptom history nor the hearing discrepancy has been resolved by the available paperwork.
